This is a hands-on workshop on making things with AI. Each week you'll learn a new concept and use it to build something: websites, writing, images, animations, music, a restaurant menu (as a website and as a PDF), data visualizations, and slide decks. We start without agents. You'll use chat-based AI tools to see what they're good at (and what they're not), learn how large language models actually work, and learn version control with Git and GitHub, which is how you'll keep track of everything an agent changes. Then we bring in AI coding agents like [Claude Code](https://www.claude.com/product/claude-code) and learn the workflow we use for the rest of the semester: the agent writes the code, you run the code, and the code builds the artifact. Going through code instead of asking the AI for the finished thing makes your work reproducible, uses far fewer tokens, and gives you much more control over the result. Along the way you'll learn to manage context and tokens, write your own agent skills, call other AI models through APIs, set up verification loops, and keep data separate from the documents it ends up in. The course ends with an individual final project of your own design.
